note: Agent Pay is not AP2. Through Verifiable Intent it uses the same four mandate vct values as AP2 v0.2 on main, with aligned constraint semantics and a mandate. key prefix; both were contributed to FIDO on 2026-04-28. No live VI use inside AP2 is documented.
Same edge pattern (RFC 9421 signature with a tag and nonce, network-hosted key directory), different tag and directory; both networks issue their own agentic tokens, which mean different products.
Indirect: Stripe Shared Payment Tokens can carry Mastercard agentic network tokens, so an ACP checkout processed by Stripe can use one. ACP itself names Mastercard only as a card brand.
Verifiable Intent says its credentials can travel in UCP's AP2 mandate extension (now dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate). Mastercard endorses UCP; no Agent Pay integration is documented.
Tempo, quoted in Mastercard's AP4M release, says it is working with Mastercard on Machine Payments Protocol compatibility; Mastercard makes no MPP claim itself and maintains no MPP payment method.
Mastercard is a premier member of the x402 Foundation, and Coinbase's AP4M quote names x402; no Agent Pay technical document mentions x402.
